item.title: Self-Hosted ZFS Management Web UIs — ZFSdash vs Cockpit ZFS Manager vs TrueNAS WebUI
item.description: Managing ZFS pools, datasets, snapshots, and encryption from the command line is powerful but can be cumbersome for day-to-day administration. Web-based ZFS management interfaces provide a visual alternative that simplifies common tasks while keeping the full power of OpenZFS underneath. In this guide, we compare three self-hosted ZFS management web UIs: ZFSdash, Cockpit ZFS Manager, and the TrueNAS WebUI.

item.title: Self-Hosted Union File Systems — SnapRAID vs MergerFS vs UnionFS-Fuse Guide 2026
item.description: Modern storage management often requires combining multiple drives of different sizes, speeds, and purposes into a single coherent view. Whether you are building a home NAS, managing a media server, or organizing backup volumes, union file systems provide the flexibility to pool heterogeneous storage without the rigidity of traditional RAID.

item.title: MiniDLNA vs Gerbera vs Rygel: Best Self-Hosted DLNA/UPnP Media Servers 2026
item.description: DLNA (Digital Living Network Alliance) and UPnP (Universal Plug and Play) protocols let you stream media from a central server to any compatible device on your network — smart TVs, game consoles, media players, and mobile apps. Instead of relying on cloud services, a self-hosted DLNA server gives you full control over your media library with zero subscription fees.

item.title: OpenMediaVault vs TrueNAS SCALE vs Rockstor: Best Self-Hosted NAS Solutions 2026
item.description: A Network Attached Storage (NAS) device is the backbone of any self-hosted home lab or small business infrastructure. Whether you are centralizing file backups, running media servers, or managing shared project files, choosing the right NAS operating system determines how easy it is to manage your storage long-term.
